claims.text: The message leg of POL-NS-23 depends solely on EV-CHAT-05066, and that artifact is IMPAIRED, not clean: its weight_multiplier is 0.85 and the issue UNREAD_MESSAGE fired (both driver messages were delivered but neither carries a read_at before cancellation). Under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence in a fact carried by that artifact cannot exceed 0.85, so the record cannot establish to full weight that the driver completed the chat-message half of the contact obligation; the fee should not be upheld on an impaired contact record.

The driver's own profile carries fraud_flags of 1 (EV-DPROF-05066), so under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 the AI ruling on this no-show is final only at a confidence of 0.95. That bar cannot be reached here, because the contact fact the fee depends on is capped at 0.85 by the impaired chat log (POL-GEN-02). The case must therefore go to human review, and on an escalated case the 5.00 SGD cancellation fee is held rather than collected -- the rider is not made to carry the disputed charge while the question is open.

POL-GEN-26 names this exact fact as one that must be escalated when the evidence carrying it is missing or impaired: 'whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling'. The only artifact carrying the message leg, EV-CHAT-05066, is graded IMPAIRED with issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE -- both messages show read_at null at delivery 20:47:02 and 20:50:21, and the single call at 20:49:30 rang 20 seconds unanswered. The open question -- whether the contact obligation was genuinely discharged to this rider, or merely attempted -- should be stated and sent to a human reviewer, with the fee held in the meantime.

The rider's account that no contact reached her is corroborated so far as the message leg goes: EV-CHAT-05066 shows delivery only, with read_at null for both MSG-05066-001 and MSG-05066-002 at the moment of cancellation, so the rider had no actual notice of the driver's presence. This does not overturn the bare fact that a call was placed -- EV-TRIP-05066 records one in-app call by the driver at 20:49:30, unanswered -- but it means the rider's statement is not a fabrication to be weighed against her, and it is a further reason the contact question belongs with a human reviewer rather than being closed on impaired evidence.

claims.text: The free-wait condition is satisfied on the trip record's own clock. The driver arrived at the pickup at 2026-09-11T20:46:45 (+08:00) and cancelled at 20:53:00, 375 seconds after arrival. The free wait under POL-NS-21 is 300 seconds and, on this on-demand trip (scheduled_at is null), runs from the driver's arrival; the wait expired at 20:51:45, so the cancellation was made after the wait had run out and was properly available to the driver.

The arrival the trip record relies on is corroborated by the driver's GPS trace, which is complete (25 fixes at 30-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gap over 120 seconds, every fix reporting horizontal accuracy). The nearest fix to the pickup point is 2.64 m away at 20:46:52 with a reported accuracy of 4 m, inside both the 25 m accuracy filter and the 50 m arrival radius that applies to a STANDARD pickup zone under POL-NS-21. The driver was physically at the pickup before the wait began.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met on both limbs, on the platform's own records. The trip record shows two in-app chat messages sent by the driver to the rider before cancellation (20:47:00 and 20:50:20) and one in-app call placed by the driver at 20:49:30, which rang for 20 seconds and was not answered, all before the 20:53:00 cancellation. POL-NS-23 requires that a message be sent and a call be placed before cancelling; it does not require that the rider read the message or answer the call. I disclose that the chat log artifact EV-CHAT-05066 is IMPAIRED, weight_multiplier 0.85, issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE (both messages were delivered but never opened); the message content therefore carries reduced weight, but the fact of sending rests also on the trip record at full weight 1.0.

The rider's central factual assertion - 'I never got any message or call' - is contradicted by the delivery receipts and the call record. Both driver messages carry a delivered_at timestamp (20:47:02 and 20:50:21), so they reached the rider's device, and the in-app call entry in the trip record (source PLATFORM_TELEMETRY, weight 1.0) shows a call placed by the driver, unanswered, at 20:49:30. The rider's account of receiving nothing is not borne out, and the call went unanswered on the rider's side of the line.

The amount charged is exactly the policy amount and is still standing. The payments ledger shows a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD charged at 20:53:04, no base, distance, time or waiting components, and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 against payment_status CHARGED. Under POL-NS-22 the no-show fee is 5.00 SGD, and the record's own derived check reports fee_matches_policy as true, so there is no fee-amount discrepancy to refer.

POL-NS-24 does not assist the rider, because the premise of that clause is not present: the rider did not cancel this trip, the driver did, and the cancellation came after the free wait had expired rather than because the driver had failed to arrive. The GPS trace shows the driver stationary at the pickup from 20:46:52 through the last fix at 20:52:52, so the arrival limb of POL-NS-24 fails. The 5.00 SGD goodwill credit attached to that clause is conditional on the driver both failing to arrive on time and failing to attempt contact; neither is true here, so no credit is owed and no referral under POL-NS-24 arises.

On the fraud flag I am candid: driver_profile.fraud_flags is 1, which under POL-GEN-22 raises the confidence an AI ruling on this dispute must reach to 0.95. That flag does not decide this trip - POL-GEN-01 confines it to the confidence threshold, and POL-GEN-22 itself says it never decides the trip. What decides the trip is the trip-level evidence, and that evidence is complete and at full weight: the arrival is GPS-corroborated (EV-GPS-05066, weight 1.0), the contact is recorded in the trip record (EV-TRIP-05066, weight 1.0), the free wait is satisfied and the fee matches policy (EV-FARE-05066, weight 1.0). The rider's insinuation that the driver 'does this to collect fees' is speculation about a pattern, not evidence about this trip, and no such pattern is established on this record.

The missing traffic-data artifact EV-ADVIS-05066-01 (status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) supplies no fact and is not needed by any rule in play. The determinations this case turns on are whether the driver arrived (carried by the GPS trace and trip record), whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling (carried by the trip record and chat log), and what fee was charged (carried by the ledger). None of them depends on a traffic advisory, so its absence leaves no open question and gives no ground for escalation under POL-GEN-26.

This no-show fee stands and the ruling should be DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD to the driver. The conditions of POL-NS-22 are met: the driver cancelled after the free wait, the rider was not on board, the 5.00 SGD no-show fee was charged to the rider, and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so nothing has yet moved back to the rider. POL-NS-22 licenses DRIVER_COMPENSATION where the fee stands, and POL-GEN-03 provides that in that ruling amount_sgd carries the same figure as driver_compensation_sgd - here 5.00 SGD in both fields. The rider's NO_ACTION alternative would leave the money exactly where it is, which is the same thing on this record; the fee is not a windfall but the compensation POL-NS-22 assigns to the driver for time and fuel spent waiting.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on the money. A single no-show cancellation fee of 5.00 SGD was charged on TRP-05066 at 20:53:04, with no base, distance, time or waiting component, and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00 (EV-FARE-05066, weight 1.0). The rider filed, disputing that 5.00 SGD charge.

What the record does establish. The driver arrived at the pickup at 20:46:45, and the arrival is corroborated by the GPS trace (EV-GPS-05066, weight 1.0): the nearest fix is 2.64 m from the pickup at 20:46:52 with a reported accuracy of 4 m, inside both the 25 m accuracy filter and the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD pickup, with 25 fixes at 30 s and no gap over 120 s. This was an on-demand trip (scheduled_at null), so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait ran from arrival, expiring at 20:51:45; the driver cancelled at 20:53:00, 375 s after arrival (EV-TRIP-05066, weight 1.0). The call half of the driver's POL-NS-23 contact obligation is on the platform record (one in-app call at 20:49:30, unanswered, 20 s). The fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes and matches policy, so no fee-amount referral arises. POL-NS-24 does not help the rider: its premise is a driver who failed to arrive, and this driver arrived, so no goodwill credit and no referral under that clause. The absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05066-01, weight 0.0) carries no fact and no rule in play needs it, so its absence raises no question.

Where the case cannot be closed. The message half of POL-NS-23 rests on the chat log EV-CHAT-05066, which is impaired: weight_multiplier 0.85, issue UNREAD_MESSAGE (MSG-05066-001 and MSG-05066-002 were delivered at 20:47:02 and 20:50:21 but never read before cancellation). The trip record does not independently carry that fact as the driver's claim asserts: its message count is the same chat data, and its derived contact block cites EV-CHAT-05066 for message_count and obligation_met, so the trip record and the chat log are one carrier at 0.85, not two. That caps confidence in the contact obligation at 0.85. The driver's profile carries fraud_flags 1, so POL-GEN-22 (carried into no-shows by POL-NS-26) requires a confidence of 0.95. 0.85 is below that bar, and the AI ruling therefore cannot be finalised in either direction: the driver's showing that the fee stands is factually strong but cannot be concluded at the confidence the fraud flag demands, and the rider's two surviving points - that the message leg is capped at 0.85, and that POL-GEN-26 leaves open whether the contact obligation was genuinely discharged - are well founded. The fraud flag does not itself decide the trip and is not used as a ground for the outcome (POL-GEN-01); it only sets the 0.95 bar.

Outcome. ESCALATE: the case goes to a human reviewer and the 5.00 SGD is held, neither collected nor refunded; both money fields are null and ESCALATE is terminal. No referral fires: POL-NS-24 (no goodwill credit - the driver arrived), POL-NS-25 (the rider's repeat-no-show counter is not present on the profile), POL-NS-22 (the fee charged is exactly 5.00 SGD). Open question for the reviewer: whether the driver's in-app contact genuinely discharged the POL-NS-23 obligation to this rider, given both messages were delivered but never opened and the single call went unanswered.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: the AI cannot close this one, so the 5.00 SGD cancellation fee is held — neither collected nor refunded — and a human reviewer will decide.

What the record does establish. The driver reached Block 115, Yishun Ring Road, at 20:46:45 on 11 Sep (POL-NS-21). The GPS trace corroborates it: the nearest fix is 2.64 m from the pickup, reporting 4 m accuracy, inside the 25 m accuracy filter and the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD zone — the arrival the trip record relies on is good. This is an on-demand trip, so the 300-second free wait ran from arrival and expired at 20:51:45; the driver cancelled at 20:53:00, 375 seconds after arrival, i.e. after the wait. The fee applied at 20:53:04 is 5.00 SGD, exactly the policy no-show fee (POL-NS-22), and the ledger shows 0.00 refunded.

Where it breaks down. POL-NS-23 requires the driver to have sent an in-app chat message AND placed an in-app call before cancelling. The call limb is solid — one in-app call at 20:49:30, unanswered, carried on the trip record at weight 1.0 — and POL-NS-23 does not require you to answer it, rider. The message limb, however, is recorded only in the chat log EV-CHAT-05066, and that artifact is impaired: weight_multiplier 0.85, issue UNREAD_MESSAGE (both messages delivered but never opened). The trip record's count of those same messages is taken from that same chat log, so it does not independently corroborate the sending; under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence in that fact is capped at 0.85.

Why that matters here. The driver's profile carries a fraud flag (fraud_flags = 1), so POL-GEN-22 (with POL-NS-26) requires a confidence of 0.95 for an AI ruling on this no-show. The deciding fact is capped at 0.85, below that bar, so the case escalates under POL-GEN-22/POL-NS-26; and the impaired contact record also leaves open the very question POL-GEN-26 names — whether the contact obligation was genuinely discharged rather than merely attempted. The 5.00 SGD is held; no money moves.

Rider: your account that you got no message or call is not borne out on the sending side — the messages carry delivery receipts and a call was placed — and the clause does not require that you read or answer. But the impaired message record is exactly why the AI will not close this case against you.

Driver: the wait, the arrival and the 5.00 SGD fee all check out, and the arrival and call sit at full weight 1.0; but the message limb rests on the impaired chat log, which caps confidence at 0.85 — below the 0.95 your own profile's fraud flag requires — so the fee cannot be confirmed by the AI and a reviewer decides.

The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05066-01, weight 0.0) is needed by no rule in play and raises no open question. No referral applies: the fee is exactly 5.00 SGD (POL-NS-22), the driver arrived and attempted contact (POL-NS-24), and the repeat no-show counter POL-NS-25 names is not present on the rider profile.

To the rider and the driver: this dispute goes to a human reviewer, so no money moves now. The SGD 5.00 no-show fee already charged to the rider is held — not collected and not refunded — until that review.

What the record establishes. The driver reached the pickup at 20:46:45 (the GPS trace puts the nearest fix 2.6 m from the pickup with 4 m reported accuracy, inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD zone under POL-NS-21) and cancelled at 20:53:00, 375 s later. On this on-demand trip the 300 s free wait runs from arrival, so it expired at 20:51:45 and the driver cancelled after it. One in-app call was placed at 20:49:30 (rang 20 s, unanswered) and two in-app messages were sent (20:47:00 and 20:50:20), all before the cancellation. The amount charged was exactly SGD 5.00, matching the POL-NS-22 fee, with refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

On the merits the fee would stand and POL-NS-22 would give DRIVER_COMPENSATION of SGD 5.00. What stops that is the confidence the policy requires. The message half of the POL-NS-23 contact obligation is carried only by the chat log EV-CHAT-05066, and that artifact is impaired: weight_multiplier 0.85, issue UNREAD_MESSAGE (both messages delivered but never opened). The trip record repeats the message count but takes that count from the same chat log, so it is not an independent source, and the call half alone does not satisfy POL-NS-23, which needs a message AND a call. Under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence in the contact fact cannot exceed 0.85.
